theViabilityVerdict:
ASKED AND ANSWERED 2026-09-07: THE TOPIC IS VIABLE, AND IT IS BETTER SOURCED THAN EITHER halal OR wine-bars. But it is viable because of one find, and without that find the honest answer would have been no.

WHAT THE PASS ACTUALLY DELIVERS - 11 distinct domains:
  TIER A  2  Fried Chicken Championships 2026, Wing Fest UK
  TIER B  6  Time Out, The Infatuation, Evening Standard, SquareMeal, The London Economic, Eater London
  TIER C  3  Hungry Soles, Secret London (two pages, ONE source), Ideal Magazine (borderline)
  TIER D  COLLECTABLE - see theApifyCorrection. This is the first topic in this batch where it is.
  TIER E  blocked. Reddit refuses curl and the browser alike.

THE FIND THAT MADE IT VIABLE. The brief expected 'two mastheads and a pile of SEO farms', and that is what the first SERP looks like. A judged, dated, national award exists and nobody has recorded it: the FRIED CHICKEN CHAMPIONSHIPS, inaugural January 2026, four judges scoring across five criteria. Its results page is at /fried-chicken-champions - NOT /winners, NOT /results, both of which 404. That is trap 6, and one wrong guess at a slug would have produced a config saying 'no award exists for this topic'.

THE FARM DENSITY IS THE WORST RECORDED ON ANY TOPIC, and this is the real hazard rather than thinness. SEVEN domains failed the blog-vs-SEO-farm test, and the worst of them ranks FIRST for two of the five queries. chickenbible.com has no byline, no date, US spellings on a London page, and lists 'Chicken Shop' five separate times and 'Thunderbird Fried Chicken' five separate times in one article - it is a scraped delivery-platform dump wearing a guide's clothes, and it outranks Time Out. A pass that trusted SERP position would have built this guide out of it.

SO THE HONEST SHAPE: real editorial opinion exists and can be measured, but it is a SHALLOW pool with a very deep farm sitting on top of it. Nine or ten real voices is enough for a consensus. It is not enough to survive a single mis-tiered farm, so the excludeOnSight list below is load-bearing, not housekeeping.
theApifyCorrection:
APIFY_TOKEN IS SET AND IT WORKS. VERIFIED 2026-09-07. data/topics/halal.json and data/topics/wine-bars.json both say it is not set, and both were written the same day. They are wrong.

WHAT WAS CHECKED: .env.local carries APIFY_TOKEN with a 46-character value. A free read-only call to https://api.apify.com/v2/users/me returns HTTP 200 for account 'foot_trombone' on the FREE plan. No actor was run and nothing was billed.

WHY THE OTHER CONFIGS GOT IT WRONG: the token is in .env.local and NOT in the shell environment, so `echo $APIFY_TOKEN` returns empty and a script that reads process.env without loading .env.local sees nothing. The blocker is dotenv loading, not a missing credential.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS. Tier D is collectable on this topic, which is the difference between passing the source-mix floor and failing it. Fried chicken is among the most heavily filmed London food subjects on YouTube and TikTok - the video tier here is not a formality, it is where the shops outside zone 2 live, and it is the only tier that reaches the chicken-shop end at all. SKILL.md budgets a topic's video tier at $1-2; the FREE plan's monthly credit covers that, so check the remaining credit before the run rather than assuming.

SOMEONE SHOULD ALSO FIX halal.json AND wine-bars.json, and re-run their video tiers. That is out of scope here and is recorded so it is not lost.
theScopeRuling:
ONE GUIDE, SECTIONED. NOT TWO. The chicken-shop question was the interesting one and the evidence came back clearly against splitting it out.

THE THREE TESTS THE wine-bars CONFIG USED TO JUSTIFY A SEPARATE GUIDE. All three fail here, in the same direction:

  1. IS IT A DIFFERENT SERP? NO. 'best chicken shop london' and 'best fried chicken london' return the SAME top ten with the SAME page at number one - Time Out's fried chicken guide. Wine bars and cocktail bars shared not one result; these share almost all of them. Where the market has already merged two intents, they are one intent, and SKILL.md forbids two pages competing for one query.

  2. ARE THEY DIFFERENT VENUES? NO. Morley's is on Time Out, The Infatuation, the Standard, Eater, Secret London, The London Economic and Hungry Soles - every general fried chicken list in the corpus. The overlap is near-total, not marginal.

  3. DO THE SOURCES THEMSELVES SPLIT THEM? NO, AND THIS IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE. Time Out's ranked eight runs Korean (CheeMc at number one), Taiwanese (Good Friend), chicken shop (Morley's), American (Butchies, Lucky's), Indian (Kricket) and modern British (Fowl) in ONE list. The Infatuation's 17 adds Malaysian, Guyanese, Caribbean, Sichuan and Thai. And The London Economic, whose headline is 'London's best chicken shops', ranks Chick'n'Sours, Butchies, Thunderbird and Absurd Bird alongside Morley's, Chicken Cottage, Favourite, Sam's and PFC. Not one publication treats the chicken shop as a separate population.

AND THERE IS NO SECOND CONSENSUS TO MEASURE ANYWAY. The chicken-shop-specific search does return a real and distinctive body of writing - the London Museum's collection piece, a BBC News feature on Morley's cult status, The Sociological Review, Culted - but it is CULTURAL WRITING, not ranking. None of it names a best. A consensus guide counts who names what; a corpus of essays about what Morley's means to south London has nothing to count. That is an argument for a section with real editorial voice in it, and against a second ranked guide.

SO: ONE page. The chicken shop gets its own SECTION (see sectionPlan) because it is a different reader arriving at the same page, and the cultural sources are worth reading before writing it even though they cannot be counted.

THE KOREAN LEG IS DIFFERENT, AND IT IS A TRAP 13 DECISION - see theOverlapFinding.
theOverlapFinding:
TRAP 13 CHECKED 2026-09-07 against korean, burgers, cheap-eats, street-food, late-night, chains, japanese, chinese, thai and new-openings. There is no american.json - the topic does not exist on this site.

URL COLLISION: NONE. Not one of the eleven seed URLs in data/serp/fried-chicken.txt appears in any consensus file. Safe to seed.

VENUE OVERLAP IS THE SMALLEST OF ANY RECENT TOPIC - and that is the finding. Of roughly 60 venues these sources name, only SIX are already recorded anywhere:
  korean.json    CheeMc, Chick and Beers, KoKoDoo, On The Bab, Wing Wing, Tongdak, Out Fry, Jinjuu, Seoul Bird
  chinese.json   Good Friend Chicken, Bunsik
  thai.json      Fortune Fried Chicken (THIRD PLACE at the 2026 Championships), Khao Bird
  japanese.json  Humble Chicken
  chains.json    Nando's
  late-night.json Smoking Goat, Dover Street Counter
  cheap-eats.json Rudie's (as a dish, 'Roti jerk chicken wrap at Rudie's')
burgers.json, street-food.json and cheap-eats.json contain NO fried chicken venue at all. Neither Wingmans nor Coqfighter nor Butchies nor Morley's nor Chick'n'Sours nor Thunderbird is recorded anywhere on this site. The entire American and chicken-shop population is new.

THE KOREAN DECISION, WHICH A HUMAN SHOULD MAKE BEFORE COLLECTION. korean.json already holds TWO sources scoped 'korean-chicken':
  DesignMyNight, best-korean-fried-chicken-london - 3 names (Chick And Beers, CheeMC, Naru)
  LondonBest, /korean-fried-chicken/ - 12 names
Do NOT re-fetch either URL under this topic - that is the exact error that put an identical ice cream URL in two corpora. Two defensible options:
  (a) LEAVE THEM IN korean.json, and let this corpus count Korean venues only where a GENERAL fried chicken source names them. CheeMc would still be strong here - Time Out ranks it number one and The Infatuation, Eater and the Standard all name it. RECOMMENDED: it keeps each corpus internally honest and it is the lower-risk option.
  (b) MIGRATE both records here, and cross-link the Korean guide instead.
Either way TRAP 7 IS THE LIVE RISK. CheeMc's korean.json citation count must NEVER appear on this page. Rebuild against topics.includes('fried-chicken') only, and check it before printing a single number.

SAME RULE FOR Fortune Fried Chicken (thai.json), Good Friend Chicken (chinese.json), Humble Chicken (japanese.json) and Smoking Goat (late-night.json). All four may legitimately sit in both corpora. None of their existing counts may be reprinted here.
theCountingProblem:
A PUB THAT DOES GOOD WINGS IS NOT A FRIED CHICKEN RESTAURANT, AND THIS IS NOT A HYPOTHETICAL - IT IS WHAT THE MOST RECENTLY UPDATED SOURCE ON THE SERP ACTUALLY IS.

DesignMyNight's 'Over 20 Best Fried Chicken Restaurants In London' was refreshed on 18 August 2026, more recently than anything else found. Its sixteen entries are Camden BBQ, Market Place Harrow, Cocotte Shoreditch, Maxwell's Bar & Grill, The Plough Clapham, Little Bat, Prince of Peckham, The Star of Bethnal Green, ALL STAR LANES BOWLING ALLEYS, BREWDOG, The Breakfast Club, Louie's, Casa do Frango, Ninth Ward and Randy's Wing Bar. Fifteen of sixteen are bars, pubs or a bowling alley that happen to sell wings. Recording it would put a tenpin bowling chain in a fried chicken guide, and DesignMyNight is registered tier C so every one of them would have counted. It is assessed and NOT seeded; the reason is in data/serp/fried-chicken.txt so nobody re-adds it.

bestdishesat.com does the same thing at the top end: it lists THE CLOVE CLUB, a tasting-menu restaurant, under fried chicken.

THE TEST. Three questions, TWO OF THREE to be counted:
  1. WOULD THE BUSINESS SURVIVE WITHOUT IT? Take fried chicken off the menu tomorrow. Does the place still have a reason to exist? Kricket does. Butchies does not. This is the question that does the most work and it is the one to ask first.
  2. IS IT IN THE NAME OR THE VENUE'S OWN WORDS? 'fried chicken', 'chicken shop', 'wings', 'hot chicken', 'KFC' in the Korean sense. Self-description wins, the same rule french.json uses for cuisine boundaries.
  3. CAN YOU EAT A WHOLE MEAL OF IT, AT A COUNTER, WITHOUT BOOKING? The chicken-shop test, and the one a reader actually applies at 11pm.

AND ONE ABSOLUTE RULE THAT IS NOT PART OF THE THREE: IT HAS TO BE FRIED. Nando's and Casa do Frango are GRILLED. Piri-piri over coals is not fried chicken, and rotisserie is not fried chicken. This matters because DuckDuckGo's own local pack returns NANDO'S AS THE NUMBER ONE RESULT for 'best fried chicken london', and Nando's is already carried in chains.json. A guide that lets it in has stopped being about its own subject. Soho House's 'Chicken Shop' brand is likewise a ROTISSERIE - and it will also collide with the category word 'chicken shop' once norm() strips the spaces, so watch for it twice.

THE HARDEST VENUE IN THE TOPIC IS CHICK'N'SOURS, AND IT BREAKS THE TEST RATHER THAN FAILING IT. It came JOINT SECOND at the 2026 Championships, tied on points with Butchies across four judges, and it appears on the Standard, Eater, Secret London, The London Economic and Hungry Soles. It also has no restaurant. Its own site, read 2026-09-07: 'Over its 10-year run as a full-on restaurant... now we're back where we belong: popping up at residencies, a network of delivery kitchens, and lighting up festival fields.' What exists today is three PUB RESIDENCIES (Crown & Castle Dalston, Big Chill King's Cross, Corner Corner Canada Water), FIVE DELIVEROO-ONLY kitchens (Kilburn, Finchley, Fulham, Peckham, Walthamstow) and a festival truck. It passes all three questions and there is nowhere to send a reader. See openVenueQuestions - this is a human decision and it decides how at least three other entries are handled.

TRAP 17 APPLIES TO IT TOO: chickenbible lists it as 'Chick n Sours @ Big Chill', which is the residency filed under its host, exactly the Crisp Pizza shape. Decide the canonical name a reader books under before anything is recorded.

awardBodies.name: Fried Chicken Championships
awardBodies.verified: 2026-09-07 - CONFIRMED LIVE AND JUDGED. Results page read in the browser. Inaugural edition January 2026. The site's own words: 'Despite four judges scoring across five different criteria, the two silver medallists finished the day on the exact same number of points.' Next edition 19 January 2027 at Big Penny Social, London.
awardBodies.note:
READ THIS BEFORE COLLECTING - THE SLUG IS THE WHOLE POINT. /winners, /results, /awards, /judges, /shortlist and /finalists ALL RETURN 404. The results live at /fried-chicken-champions, linked from the nav. Trap 6: this award would have been written off as 'no published results page' by anyone who guessed at slugs, and the config would have said no judged award exists for this topic.

2026 RESULTS AS PUBLISHED:
  CHAMPION            20Ft Fried Chicken (Stewart Down) - the 20Ft Hot Chicken Burger
  JOINT SECOND        Chick'N'Sours AND Butchies - tied on points
  THIRD               Fortune Fried Chicken - Nam Jim Chicken Tenders, sister brand to Gunpowder
  PERFECT PLATTER     Sides (Gordon McDermott), the Sidemen's brand
  LOADED FRIES        Killa Waffles (Alex Gaffke), Nashville-style loaded fries
  BLOGGERS' CHOICE    Butchies - Kimchi Honey Butter Tenders

FOUR HANDLING RULES.
(1) IT AWARDS A DISH, NOT A ROOM. 'Stewart Down's 20Ft Hot Chicken Burger will be the dish to try this year.' Record the dish in the quote; the citation attaches to the venue.
(2) SCOPE IT (trap 12). It is a UK-wide trade competition. Establish where each winner actually trades before counting - Sides is a virtual brand with no address, and Killa Waffles needs checking.
(3) ONE YEAR OF RESULTS ONLY. Inaugural. There is no back catalogue and no trend, so it cannot carry a 'perennial winner' claim.
(4) IT IS A TRADE COMPETITION, run by H2O Publishing (Quick Serve Magazine) and sponsored by foodservice suppliers - AAK, Lamb Weston, Meadowvale, Americana, Paulig, Valentine. Operators enter. That is the SAME SHAPE as the National Pizza Awards, which this project already carries as tier A, so it is consistent to count it - but it means the field is who entered, not who is best, and the guide should not imply otherwise.

SYNDICATION WARNING (trap 2). Time Out, MyLondon, The Times, Ham & High, Dine Out and Quick Serve all reported this result. The AWARD is the source. None of those write-ups is an independent opinion, and Time Out already counts once for its own guide.

awardBodies.name: Wing Fest UK
awardBodies.verified: 2026-09-07 - CONFIRMED LIVE. A year-picker archive running 2014-2026 with London, Sheffield and Nottingham legs, and Judges' Choice plus People's Choice across Buffalo, Wild and BBQ wings.
awardBodies.note:
REAL, JUDGED AND DATED - AND THE POPULATION IT JUDGES IS NOT THIS GUIDE'S POPULATION. Weigh it accordingly rather than counting it whole.

THE PROBLEM: it judges FESTIVAL TRADERS, not London restaurants. The 2026 London winners are Peck Peck, Ginger Wings, Mexican Seoul, Greidy's Wings & Strips, Mollis, Bare Bones, Djangos Smokehouse, Hot Chick, KYR Kitchen, Jus' Winging It and Kell's Kitchen. Several are pop-ups and market traders with no permanent site, and the field is whoever booked a pitch at a ticketed festival. This is the same shape as the Star Wine List problem recorded in wine-bars.json - a genuinely judged award whose subject is next door to the guide's subject.

THREE RULES:
(1) COUNT JUDGE'S CHOICE ONLY. People's Choice is a crowd vote and is aggregator-shaped - the exact thing the Tripadvisor rule exists to keep out.
(2) SCOPE TO THE LONDON LEG (trap 12). Sheffield and Nottingham sit on the same page behind the same picker.
(3) IT ONLY JUDGES WINGS. One format out of six in the facet axis. It says nothing about a thigh, a burger or a box, so it cannot be treated as a ranking of the topic.

WORTH READING FOR BREADTH EVEN IF LIGHTLY COUNTED: it is the only source in the whole pass that reaches street-food traders at all, and 'Peck Peck' also turns up in goodtoorder's list, so some of these do have addresses. Establish which have a permanent London site before recording any of them.

awardBodiesChecked: NO OTHER JUDGED AWARD FOUND. Searched 'fried chicken award UK judged winners 2026 takeaway' and 'Wing Fest UK winners'. The two above are the whole of tier A.

British Takeaway Awards - NOT CHECKED IN THIS PASS and worth one look before collection. If it carries a chicken category it would be judged, dated and directly on-topic, and it would reach the chicken-shop end that nothing else does.
The Sidemen's 'Sides' won a Championships category. That is a brand winning an award, not an awarding body. Do not record it as one.

editorialLists.name: Time Out
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - LIVE. Leonie Cooper, published 1 May 2026, updated 10 August 2026. The freshest masthead source in the topic.
editorialLists.note:
IT IS RANKED, AND ITS ENTRIES ARE DISHES RATHER THAN RESTAURANTS. The headings read '1. Honey butter KFC at CheeMc', '3. Spicy wings at Morley's', '5. Keralan fried chicken (KFC) at Kricket Soho'. Record the DISH in the quote and attach the citation to the venue - this is the most useful per-venue detail any source in the corpus gives, and it is exactly what SKILL.md's entry floor asks for ('the dish a reader would order').

THE RANK IS REAL - the list is numbered and ordered, unlike its halal guide. But read the caption again before recording ranks (trap 11), and note the extraction returned only the first eight headings, so the list is longer than what curl sees. Read it in the browser and get the full order.

ITS TOP EIGHT IS ALSO THE SINGLE BEST PIECE OF EVIDENCE FOR theScopeRuling: CheeMc (Korean), Good Friend (Taiwanese), Morley's (chicken shop), Butchies (American), Kricket (Indian), Lucky's Hot Chicken (Nashville), Fowl (modern British), Chick and Beers (Korean). One list, six traditions.

Time Out's news desk also reported the Fried Chicken Championships result. That is syndication and does not count again - one masthead, one opinion.

editorialLists.name: The Infatuation
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - LIVE. '17 Spots For Great Fried Chicken In London', four bylined writers (Heidi Lauth Beasley, Jake Missing, Rianne Shlebak, Daisy Meager), first published 2022 and updated 12 June 2026.
editorialLists.note:
UNRANKED - '17 Spots', a set not an order. NO RANKS FROM THIS ONE.

THE BREADTH SOURCE IN THE TOPIC, and the widest-travelled list anywhere in this pass: CheeMc, Maureen's Brixton Kitchen, Chick King, Sichuan Fry, Kaieteur Kitchen, The Best Broasted, Normah's, Manna, Tongdak New Malden, Bao, Imone, Morley's, La Barra, Kricket Soho, Smoking Goat, Good Friend, Eden's Cottage. Caribbean, Guyanese, Malaysian, Sichuan, Taiwanese, Korean, Indian and Thai in one guide, plus New Malden - which is zone 4 and outside every area guide the site has.

Several of these appear NOWHERE else in the corpus. Kaieteur Kitchen, Maureen's, Imone, Manna and The Best Broasted are single-source venues on this evidence, which is a reason to collect the video tier rather than to drop them.

editorialLists.name: Evening Standard
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - LIVE. Josh Barrie, 19 May 2025. Ten venues: Good Friend, Morley's, Koya Ko, Chick 'n' Sours, Coqfighter, Chick and Beers, Mother Clucker, Eden's Cottage, La Barra, Tonkotsu.
editorialLists.note:
A NAMED LONDON FOOD CRITIC, which makes it the most straightforwardly trustworthy source in the set. Unranked.

TWO PAGES ON THIS DOMAIN AND THEY ARE ONE SOURCE. There is an older page at /the-best-fried-chicken-shops-in-london-a3805796.html, also live. Do NOT record both - distinct domains, never URLs. Compare the name arrays first: if they are near-identical that is trap 16 and the older one is simply the same guide at an earlier URL; if they differ, merge the arrays into one record and keep both URLs in the quote.

NOTE THE HEADLINE SAYS 'chicken shops' while the list is mostly restaurants (Koya Ko is Japanese, Tonkotsu is a ramen chain). More evidence for theScopeRuling: even the mastheads use the two terms interchangeably.

editorialLists.name: SquareMeal
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - LIVE. Ellie Donnell, first published July 2019, updated 29 May 2025. Thirteen venues.
editorialLists.note:
NUMBERED IN THE HEADLINE ('13 top joints') BUT NOT ORDERED. No ranks.

THE MOST CHAIN-HEAVY LIST IN THE CORPUS, and useful precisely for that: Chicken Shop, Popeyes, Slim Chickens, Bao, Kricket, Butchies, Thunderbird, Patty & Bun, Coqfighter - nine of thirteen are multi-branch. It also names Tanakatsu (Angel) and FOWL by Fallow, which few others do.

THREE HANDLING NOTES. Its entries are branch-specific in the structured data ('Butchies Shoreditch', 'Patty & Bun James Street', 'Chicken Shop Soho') while the headings are brand-level ('Butchies, Various London locations') - decide the canonical level before recording, per chains.json. 'Chicken Shop' here is the Soho House ROTISSERIE brand and probably fails the fried test. And Patty & Bun is a burger restaurant, so run the three-question test on it.

editorialLists.name: The London Economic
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - LIVE. Jack Peat, 3 July 2023, updated 7 August 2023. Ranked 1-11.
editorialLists.note:
THE ONLY RANKED CHICKEN-SHOP LIST THAT EXISTS, and the second of only two ordered sources in the whole topic. Worth having for that alone.

RANKED ORDER AS PUBLISHED: 1 Morley's, 2 Chicken Cottage, 3 Chick 'n' Sours, 4 Butchies, 5 Favourite, 6 Sam's Chicken, 7 Perfect Fried Chicken (PFC), 8 Chicken Town, 9 Absurd Bird, 10 Thunderbird Fried Chicken, 11 Chicken Shop.

SCOPE IT BEFORE COUNTING - IT RANKS CHAINS, NOT SHOPS. Its own standfirst says 'Head to one of these top chicken shop chains'. Every entry is a brand with many branches, so no citation here attaches to a single address, and chains.json handling applies to all eleven.

IT IS ALSO THE THIRD SOURCE TO PROVE theScopeRuling: a list headlined 'chicken shops' that ranks Chick'n'Sours third and Butchies fourth, above Sam's and PFC. The publications do not hold the two categories apart.

THREE YEARS OLD. Chick 'n' Sours has since stopped being a restaurant and Absurd Bird's London presence needs checking before either is printed.

editorialLists.name: Eater London
editorialLists.verified: 2026-09-07 - PAGE IS LIVE BUT IT IS FOUR YEARS OLD. The visible stamp reads 'Updated Jun 27, 2022'; the JSON-LD carries updatedAt: null. Twelve venues: Chick King, Eden's Cottage, The Best Broasted, Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen, Chick 'n' Sours, Koya Ko Hackney, Butchies Shoreditch, Good Friend Chicken, BAO Borough, La Barra, Rooster's Hut, Morley's Fried Chicken. By Jonathan Hatchman.
editorialLists.note:
BORDERLINE - INCLUDE OR DROP IS A HUMAN DECISION, AND IT IS NOT A SILENT ONE. Same shape as the Halal Food Guy Top 100 problem in halal.json: a real masthead, a real byline, and a list old enough to carry closed restaurants.

FOR: it is a tier-B voice in a topic with only six, it is a proper Eater map with per-venue prose, and it is the only source besides the Standard naming Koya Ko and the only one besides Secret London naming Rooster's Hut.
AGAINST: June 2022, Eater London has since stopped publishing so it will never be updated, and it names Chick 'n' Sours - which no longer has a restaurant - as a place to go.

IF KEPT, mark it as a 2022 source in the quote and check every one of its twelve is still trading before a single name reaches print. If dropped, record that here so the next pass does not re-add it.

independentSources.name: Hungry Soles
independentSources.verified: 2026-09-07 - LIVE AND CURRENTLY PUBLISHING. Named writer Zaeem Jafri. Post first published March 2024, updated September 2025; the site's latest posts are dated 2 September 2026. NEW DOMAIN - register it in data/sources.json as tier C.
independentSources.note:
THE ONLY UNAMBIGUOUS BLOG IN THE TOPIC, and it PASSED the README's test on every count: named writer, British spelling, original visit language, and - the tell that settles it - a section headed 'The ones that missed the cut...' naming Coqfighter and Chick 'n' Sours. A scraper does not exclude things. It also publishes a fried chicken MAP of London.

IT NAMES VENUES NOBODY ELSE DOES: Dixy Chicken and Other Side Fried appear on no other list in the pass, and it covers Fowl, Thunderbird, Butchies, Patty and Bun, Morley's, Lucky's Hot Chicken and Meat Liquor.

AND IT IS THE ONLY SOURCE ANYWHERE THAT PRINTS HALAL STATUS PER VENUE - a bare 'Halal' line against Dixy Chicken, Other Side Fried, Thunderbird and Morley's. That is genuinely useful and it must NOT be treated as certification. It labels Morley's 'Halal' while Morley's own site says 'halal friendly options', which is precisely the status-2 versus status-3 conflation data/topics/halal.json documents, caught in the wild on this topic. Use it as a lead to check, never as the answer. See theHalalNote.

independentSources.name: Secret London
independentSources.verified: 2026-09-07 - LIVE. Samuel Hopkins. Fried chicken page written 17 January 2023, last touched 24 April 2023 - the oldest source in the topic. Wings page updated 25 April 2025.
independentSources.note:
TWO PAGES, ONE SOURCE. MERGE THE ARRAYS. Already registered tier C in data/sources.json and already used on halal, turkish and middle-eastern under other URLs.
  /best-fried-chicken-london/ - 10 names: Coqfighter, Smoking Goat Chicken Shop, Chick 'n' Sours, Chick and Beers, Mother Clucker, Rooster's Hut, Morley's Fried Chicken, Chick King, La Barra, Eden's Cottage
  /chicken-wings-london/ - 8 names: Chick and Beers, Wingmans, Chick 'n' Sours, Supawan Thai Food, Mother Clucker, Wingstop, Coqfighter, Butchies

THE WINGS PAGE EARNS ITS PLACE: it is the ONLY source in the entire pass that names WINGMANS, and the only one naming Wingstop. Wingmans is one of the best-known fried chicken names in London and it appears on no masthead list here at all - either the mastheads have quietly dropped it or the corpus has a hole, and that is worth resolving explicitly rather than letting a one-source count bury it.

BOTH PAGES ARE NUMBERED AND NEITHER IS ORDERED - a curated sequence, same as its halal list. No ranks. And the fried chicken page is three and a half years old, so check its venues are trading.

independentSources.name: Ideal Magazine
independentSources.verified: 2026-09-07 - LIVE. Joseph Gann, 3 June 2025, touched again 27 August 2026. Twelve venues: Smoking Goat, Chick-King, Other Side Fried, Manna, Chick 'n' Sours, BAO, Good Friend Chicken, Sichuan Fry, Kricket, Butchies, Popeyes, Morley's.
independentSources.note:
BORDERLINE-IN, and the reasoning is recorded so it is not re-argued.

FOR: a named writer, British spelling, and one detail that proves somebody checked rather than scraped - it annotates its own entry, 'Chick 'n' Sours, Haggerston & Seven Dials *as of June 2025, now sadly closed*'. A farm does not correct itself mid-list. It is also one of only two sources naming Other Side Fried and one of three naming Sichuan Fry.

AGAINST: it is not a London food publication. Its entire recent output is Penang street food - ten consecutive 'Ideal Eats' posts from George Town and Tanjung Tokong. A general lifestyle magazine writing one London listicle is a weaker voice than a London blog, and the README's line for business blogs is 'local and relevant'.

IT IS IN because the topic cannot afford to lose a tier-C voice and the page carries real per-venue judgement. If a later pass finds it aggregating, drop it AND note the drop here.

assessedAndExcluded.verdict: EXCLUDE. THE WORST PAGE FOUND ON ANY SERP FOR THIS TOPIC, AND IT RANKS NUMBER ONE FOR TWO OF THE FIVE QUERIES.
assessedAndExcluded.finding: Fails on five named tells at once. NO BYLINE and NO DATE anywhere on a 3,528-word page. US SPELLINGS on a London subject - 'favorite', 'flavor', 'neighborhood' - including the venue name rendered as 'Favorite Chicken & Ribs' when the British chain is Favourite. And the structure gives it away completely: 108 headings in which 'Chicken Shop' appears FIVE separate times, 'Thunderbird Fried Chicken' FIVE times (once as 'Thunderbird Fried chicken'), and 'Perfect Chicken' twice. That is a delivery-platform or Places listing dump paginated into a guide, not an article. It also lists 'Chick 'n' Sours @ Big Chill' as its own venue, which is trap 17 committed by a machine. Do not seed any chickenbible URL, including its separate wings page.

assessedAndExcluded.verdict: EXCLUDE - ALREADY EXCLUDED ON wine-bars, 2026-09-07, and it appears here TWICE (a fried chicken page and a wings page), both in the top three. The reason stands: no named writer, and the page discloses that the site is 'part of the same group as Cleopatra Agency, a distinguished London companionship service'. An escort agency's nightlife guide is not a food publication. Recorded again here because it is now on its second topic and someone will meet it a third time.

EXCLUDE. No byline, no date, US spellings ('favorite', 'flavor', 'savor'), and ONE heading on the whole page - the h1. The venue names exist only in structured data, which is what a generated page looks like. Its list does contain real and unusual names (That Wing Place, Taikula Fried Chicken, Peck Peck), so it is worth reading once as a LEAD on venues to search for elsewhere. It is not a source.

EXCLUDE. Programmatic comparison-page generator. 'Best Fried Chicken in London - 14 Restaurants Compared', no date, and the same venue repeated as separate entries: 'Monga' five times, 'Good Friend Chicken' three times, 'Morley's' twice. It lists THE CLOVE CLUB, a tasting-menu restaurant, under fried chicken. It also attaches an author credential - 'Paolo Rosson, University of Oxford, PhD in Atomic & Laser Physics' - to a restaurant listicle, which is a trust signal manufactured rather than earned.

EXCLUDE. A US recipe blog publishing a London listicle. The article byline reads 'George Robinson' while the sidebar of the same page reads 'Welcome, I'm Keri' above a 'Cozy Soups' section - two identities and a US spelling in the furniture. US spellings in the body too ('flavor', 'neighborhood'). The list is the proof: alongside real venues it names 'Cluckin' Bell', which is a restaurant from the Grand Theft Auto games, and 'GBK Fried Chicken Burger', which is a menu item.

EXCLUDE - AND IT IS TRAP 12 IN ITS PUREST FORM. 'The Best Wings in London: A City-Wide Guide to Where the Locals Actually Go' ranks in the UK top ten for 'best wings london 2026'. It is LONDON, ONTARIO. Verified 2026-09-07: its venue addresses read '1165 Oxford St E, London, ON N5Y 3L7, Canada', '390 Springbank Dr, London, ON'. Recording it would have put Canadian wing bars in a London guide with a straight face. Any 'London' source must have its country checked, not just its city.

EXCLUDE. Not editorial. 'The 10 Best Chicken Shops in London' is a directory page that says 'found 310 companies' and offers sibling categories with counts - Fast Food Restaurants 2131, Fried Chicken Takeaways 638. A filterable business database, no byline, no reviews. Same class as Tripadvisor and Yelp, both of which also ranked on these SERPs.

EXCLUDE ITS CHICKEN PAGES, and note the reason is unusual. MyLondon is a real regional masthead with named staff, so this is NOT a farm exclusion. Its chicken coverage is 'The best Morley's in every London borough according to Google reviews' - a ranking DERIVED FROM GOOGLE REVIEW SCORES, which is a crowd aggregate wearing a masthead's byline, and it ranks branches of ONE brand against each other rather than venues against each other. Neither is an independent editorial opinion. Its news reporting of the Championships result is syndication (trap 2). If a MyLondon page turns up that is a real first-person guide, that one may count.

ASSESSED, LIVE, AND DELIBERATELY NOT SEEDED. Registered tier C in data/sources.json and updated 18 August 2026, so it would have been an easy include. Its sixteen 'best fried chicken restaurants' are bars, pubs and a BOWLING ALLEY - see theCountingProblem for the full list. Also note it publishes a SECOND chicken wings page; if a human overrules this and seeds it, the two pages are ONE source. And DesignMyNight has already contributed pure chrome twice in bars.json, which is a separate reason for caution.
EXCLUDE - already on both the permanent403 and excluded lists in data/sources.json. Ranked on the wings SERP.

TIER F, NOT A SOURCE. It ranks third for 'best chicken shop london' and it is the Soho House brand's own site. A venue recommending itself is excluded at collection. It is also a ROTISSERIE, so it may not belong in the guide as a venue either.
Aggregators, already excluded globally. All three ranked on the wings SERP.

theSourceMixVerdict:
THE FLOOR IS REACHABLE ON THIS TOPIC. That is the first time in this batch of configs, and it is worth being precise about why, because the reason is a mistake in the other two files rather than anything special about fried chicken.

THE FLOOR: a judged award exists (two, in fact), so scripts/audit-source-mix.mjs requires TWO independent social voices rather than three.

  TIER D (video)     AVAILABLE. APIFY_TOKEN is set in .env.local and validates - see theApifyCorrection. This alone can supply both required voices.
  TIER E (community) BLOCKED. Reddit refuses curl and the browser pane alike. Only Rob pasting thread URLs fixes it.

SO: 2 of 2 achievable, from tier D alone, and the topic can be collected and published honestly. COLLECT THE VIDEO TIER BEFORE THE ARTICLE IS DRAFTED, NOT AFTER - on pizza, 24 social sources carried places nobody had written up, and this topic needs that more than pizza did.

WHY IT NEEDS IT MORE. The published tier here is not just thin, it is CONCENTRATED IN ZONE 1-2 AND IN BRANDS. Six mastheads and three blogs cover roughly the same forty venues, and the chicken shop - which is the numerically dominant form of fried chicken in London and the reason the search volume exists - is represented almost entirely by the chains that have a marketing department. Morley's, Chicken Cottage, Sam's, PFC and Favourite are on the lists; the single-site shop on a high street in Lewisham or Tottenham is on none of them. Video is the only tier that goes there.

AND THE HONEST CAVEAT NO SCRIPT WILL CATCH. Of eleven published sources, ONE is from 2026 and current (Time Out), two are 2025, one is 2023 and one is 2022. The corpus skews old for a category that churns fast - Chick 'n' Sours alone has stopped being a restaurant since three of these were written. audit-source-mix checks tier balance, not freshness. Somebody has to check trading status venue by venue before print, and this file is the only place that says so.

SECOND CAVEAT: SEVEN DOMAINS EXCLUDED AGAINST NINE COUNTED. That is the highest failure rate recorded on any topic - wine-bars lost three of five new domains, this lost seven. The excludeOnSight list is doing more work here than anywhere else on the site, and a future pass that re-runs these searches will meet all seven again.

facetAxis.note:
THE AXIS IS THE COOKING TRADITION, and the justification is that every serious source's list ALREADY spans it while no source splits on anything else. Time Out's ranked eight runs Korean, Taiwanese, chicken shop, American, Indian and modern British; The Infatuation's 17 adds Malaysian, Guyanese, Caribbean, Sichuan and Thai. When two independent mastheads both organise the subject implicitly along one line, that line is how the reader browses it.

WHY NOT THE ALTERNATIVES, each rejected on evidence:
  PRICE - almost the whole topic is cheap. A £ / ££ split would put forty venues in one bucket. The standard 'Cheapest' section covers what is left.
  AREA - there is a chicken shop on every high street in London. An area axis carries no information here, unlike Korean where New Malden means something.
  FORMAT (counter / table / delivery) - nearly everything is counter service, so it does not split the set. Where it DOES matter it matters as a warning, and that belongs in theCountingProblem and the booking summary.
  WING VERSUS BURGER VERSUS BOX - this is a menu axis, not a venue axis. Most places do all three.

The tradition axis is also the only one under which the reader's real question - what kind of fried chicken do I want tonight - gets a different answer per value.

values.label: The chicken shop
values.describeAs: a fryer, a hatch and a laminated menu, where two wings and chips comes in a printed box and the lights are still on at midnight

values.label: American and Southern
values.describeAs: brined overnight in buttermilk, dredged and fried, then either left plain or dragged through cayenne-heavy hot oil in the Nashville way

values.label: Korean
values.describeAs: fried twice so the skin stays brittle under a soy-garlic or gochujang glaze, eaten with pickled radish and cold beer

values.label: Taiwanese and Japanese
values.describeAs: salt-and-pepper popcorn chicken thrown with fried basil leaves, or karaage marinated in soy, ginger and sake before it hits the oil

values.label: Caribbean and West African
values.describeAs: scotch bonnet in the marinade, fried hard, and served with rice and peas or jollof rather than fries

values.label: South and Southeast Asian
values.describeAs: a curry-leaf and Keralan spice batter, Thai wings glazed in fish sauce, or a Malaysian rempah worked into the crust

facetAxis.cutIfThin: The caribbean-west-african value rests on five names from two sources (Maureen's Brixton Kitchen, Kaieteur Kitchen, Eden's Cottage, The Best Broasted, Jollof Mama). If collection finishes with fewer than three, FOLD IT INTO the chicken-shop value rather than printing a two-venue section - the wine-bars sherry precedent. The video tier is the likeliest place these get a second citation, which is another reason to collect it first.

formatSection.title: Still frying at midnight
formatSection.note:
THE SECTION NOBODY PRINTS, AND THE ABSENCE IS VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Chicken shops are the late-night eating infrastructure of London - they are what is open when everything else has shut, and for a large share of the city that is the entire point of them. Nobody maps it.

THE ABSENCE, CHECKED THREE WAYS ON 2026-09-07:
  1. data/consensus/late-night.json holds 50 venues drawn from FOUR London late-night guides - The Infatuation, The Nudge, London x London and Luxury London. NOT ONE is a chicken shop. Four guides to eating late in London, and the most numerous late-opening food business in the city appears zero times.
  2. None of the five main fried chicken sources prints a single opening hour. Time Out, The Infatuation, the Standard, The London Economic and Hungry Soles were grepped for 'open until', 'past midnight', '3am', '2am', 'closes at' and 'late night'. The only hit anywhere was Hungry Soles writing 'we've spent many late nights' about Thunderbird - a memory, not a time.
  3. Morley's own website lists roughly ninety store ADDRESSES and no hours at all, on any page.

SO THE SECTION IS RIGHT AND ITS DATA IS NOT IN REACH TODAY. Say so here rather than discovering it while writing.

WHERE THE NUMBERS WOULD COME FROM. data/enrichment.json was checked - 914 records, and the fields are placeId, placesName, address, postcode, website, businessStatus, closedDays, lat, lng, ward, station, stationDistanceM, walkMin, walkFrom, bookingHint, pressChecked. There is NO closing-time field. late-night.json's own note says the same thing: 'the sheet has no closing-time column - Closed Days says which days, never how late.' Two honest routes, and a human picks:
  (a) ADD opening_hours.periods TO THE PLACES ENRICHMENT. It comes back in the same Places call the pipeline already makes for address and postcode, so this is a code change plus a re-run rather than a new class of spend - but the re-run IS THE BILLED STAGE and must not happen without Rob saying so. It would also fix late-night.json, which has wanted this column since it was written.
  (b) A BROWSER PASS PER VENUE, reading each shop's own listing.

NEVER ESTIMATE OR INFER A CLOSING TIME. A reader standing outside a shuttered shop at one in the morning is the same class of error as a dead booking link, and 'chicken shops are open late' is exactly the kind of thing that feels safe to assume and is wrong per branch. Where the hour cannot be confirmed, print the fact that it serves late WITHOUT a time, or leave the venue out of the section.

WHY NOT THE OTHER CANDIDATES:
  HALAL - rejected, and see theHalalNote. It is already the format section of halal.json, it carries a harm risk that guide is set up to handle and this one is not, and only one source here prints it at all.
  DELIVERY-ONLY GHOST KITCHENS - real and unavoidable on this topic, but it is a COUNTING question rather than a format, and it does far more work in theCountingProblem where a reader learns that the joint-second-best fried chicken in Britain has nowhere to sit.
  UNDER A FIVER - the standard article shape already carries a 'Cheapest' section. Duplicating it as the format section wastes the slot.

theHalalNote:
NOT THE FORMAT SECTION, BUT CARRY IT AS A PER-VENUE FIELD, and read data/topics/halal.json before writing a word of it.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE: a large share of London's chicken shops are halal, and for a lot of this guide's readers that is the first question, not the last. Chicken Cottage brands ITSELF 'HALAL · FRIED' on its own front page. Hungry Soles marks Dixy Chicken, Other Side Fried, Thunderbird and Morley's as halal.

WHY IT IS NOT THE FORMAT SECTION, in order:
  1. halal.json ALREADY has 'Certified, self-declared, or halal options only' as its format section. Two guides printing the same section is a waste of the slot on one of them.
  2. halal.json's theAccuracyProblem applies in full: getting this wrong is a harm, not a ranking error, because a reader is relying on it for a religious dietary requirement. That guide is built to carry the risk; this one is not.
  3. THE CONFLATION IS ALREADY HAPPENING IN THIS CORPUS. Hungry Soles prints a flat 'Halal' against Morley's. Morley's own site says 'halal friendly OPTIONS'. That is status 2 being reported as status 1, on the biggest name in the topic, by the best blog in the corpus - the precise failure halal.json documents, found in the wild here.

SO: record halal status per venue where a venue's OWN site or a certifier's register confirms it, sourced to whoever says it, never upgraded from a listicle, and marked 'unconfirmed' otherwise. Cross-link the halal guide rather than re-arguing the axis. A one-line cross-reference is worth more to that reader than a section built on a blog's shorthand.
sectionPlan:
The standard order in SKILL.md, with two topic-specific notes.

SECTION 1 - THE WINNERS. There ARE real rankings here, which halal and wine-bars did not have: the Fried Chicken Championships 2026 (champion, joint second, third) and two ordered editorial lists (Time Out, ranked; The London Economic, ranked 1-11). Lead on what won. DO NOT sort by citation count.

AND THERE IS A GENUINE DIVERGENCE TO EXPLAIN IN TWO SENTENCES. The judges' champion is 20Ft Fried Chicken, which appears on NO editorial list in the corpus except an excluded farm. Time Out's number one is CheeMc, which the award did not place. The Championships and the critics do not agree on a single name at the top, and that is the most interesting thing in the data.

THE CHICKEN SHOP SECTION is the format-specific slot in the standard order, and it is where theScopeRuling lands. Write it with the cultural sources read but not counted - the London Museum's Morley's piece, the BBC feature, The Sociological Review. They cannot be citations and they are the difference between a section that understands its subject and a list of takeaways.
knownGaps: TWO JUDGED AWARDS EXIST AND BOTH ARE NEWLY FOUND. Fried Chicken Championships 2026 - real, four judges, five criteria, but INAUGURAL, so one year of results and no trend. Wing Fest - a 2014-2026 archive, but it judges festival traders rather than London restaurants and only judges wings. Neither is a Michelin-shaped inspectorate and the guide should not imply one.

TIER E (community) CANNOT BE COLLECTED HERE - Reddit is blocked to curl and to the browser pane. It costs more on this topic than on most: which chicken shop is best is one of the genuinely argued questions in London, it is argued per postcode, and r/london is where the single-site shops that no publication has ever written up would come from. Only fix is Rob pasting thread URLs.

TIER D (video) IS AVAILABLE AND MUST NOT BE SKIPPED. See theApifyCorrection - the token is set and works, contrary to what halal.json and wine-bars.json say. Fried chicken is one of the most heavily filmed London food subjects and this is the only tier that reaches outside zone 2.

THE CORPUS SKEWS OLD. One source is current (Time Out, Aug 2026), two are 2025, Secret London's main page is 2023, The London Economic is 2023 and Eater is JUNE 2022 from a publication that no longer exists. Chick 'n' Sours stopped being a restaurant after three of them were written. Trading status has to be checked venue by venue before print.

SEVEN DOMAINS FAILED THE BLOG-VS-SEO-FARM TEST against nine that passed - the highest failure rate on any topic recorded here. The worst of them, chickenbible.com, RANKS FIRST for two of the five queries. Anyone re-running these searches will meet all seven again; the excludeOnSight list is the defence.

NO OPENING HOURS ARE PUBLISHED ANYWHERE THE FETCHER CAN REACH, which is a gap in the format section rather than in the sourcing. data/enrichment.json has closedDays and no closing time across 914 records; Morley's own site publishes ninety addresses and no hours. See formatSection for the two routes and the rule against guessing.

WINGMANS IS NAMED BY EXACTLY ONE SOURCE in this pass - Secret London's wings page - and by no masthead at all. It is one of the best-known fried chicken names in London. Either the critics have quietly moved on or the corpus has a hole; resolve it explicitly rather than letting a one-source count bury it.
BRITISH TAKEAWAY AWARDS was not checked. If it carries a chicken category it is judged, dated and reaches the chicken-shop end that nothing else in tier A does. Worth one look before collection.

halal.json AND wine-bars.json BOTH STATE THAT APIFY_TOKEN IS NOT SET. It is. Both should be corrected and both should have their video tiers re-run. Out of scope for this config, recorded so it is not lost.

Per SKILL.md and the no-weakness-lines rule: NONE of the above may be printed in the article. It lives here. If a gap is big enough that the guide would mislead without it, ask Rob or collect more - never print it.
openVenueQuestions: CHICK'N'SOURS IS THE ONE TO SETTLE FIRST, BECAUSE IT DECIDES SEVERAL OTHERS. Joint second at the 2026 Championships, tied on points with Butchies, and named by the Standard, Eater, Secret London (both pages), The London Economic and Hungry Soles - six citations. It has no restaurant. Its own site, read 2026-09-07: three pub residencies (Crown & Castle Dalston, Big Chill King's Cross, Corner Corner Canada Water), five Deliveroo-only kitchens (Kilburn, Finchley, Fulham, Peckham, Walthamstow) and a festival truck. Ideal Magazine already annotates it 'now sadly closed'. THREE QUESTIONS FOR A HUMAN: does a delivery-only kitchen count as a venue at all; if the residencies count, is the canonical name 'Chick'n'Sours' or 'Chick'n'Sours at the Crown & Castle' (trap 17, the Crisp Pizza shape); and if it is carried, does it get a booking link, given SKILL.md forbids one on a venue that takes no bookings.

SIDES - won the Perfect Platter Award at the 2026 Championships. It is the Sidemen's virtual brand and wearesides.com does not resolve. Same delivery-only question as Chick'n'Sours, decided by the same ruling.

20FT FRIED CHICKEN - THE CHAMPION, and the corpus barely knows it. Named by no editorial source in the pass except the excluded chickenbible. 20ftfriedchicken.com does not resolve to curl. Ham & High reports it as Paddington. CONFIRM THE ADDRESS AND TRADING STATUS BEFORE IT LEADS THE GUIDE - the article's section 1 rests on it.

MORLEY'S IS NOT ENTIRELY A LONDON BUSINESS. Its own store list carries roughly ninety branches, and these are NOT in London: Nottingham, Portsmouth, Brighton, Milton Keynes, Southend, Aylesbury, Hatfield, Gillingham, Sheerness, Canterbury (Aylesham), plus Woking, Swanley, Loughton, Watford and several Surrey and Kent addresses (Molesey, Epsom, Cheam, Bexley). Trap 12 at branch level. Also decide the canonical name - Eater and Secret London write 'Morley's Fried Chicken', everyone else 'Morley's' - and add it to data/name-aliases.json.

NANDO'S AND CASA DO FRANGO ARE GRILLED, NOT FRIED, and both surfaced on these searches - Nando's as DuckDuckGo's NUMBER ONE local result for 'best fried chicken london', Casa do Frango on DesignMyNight. Nando's is already carried in chains.json. Neither belongs here. Decide once and write it into the exclusion so it does not creep back in through a video source.

KRICKET, SMOKING GOAT, BAO, PATTY & BUN, TONKOTSU, THE CLOVE CLUB, DOVER STREET COUNTER, HUMBLE CHICKEN - restaurants with a famous fried chicken dish rather than fried chicken restaurants. Kricket is the sharpest: Time Out ranks its Keralan fried chicken FIFTH, and The Infatuation, SquareMeal and Ideal all name it. Run the three-question test on each and write the answer here rather than deciding silently. Smoking Goat and Dover Street Counter are already in late-night.json and Humble Chicken is in japanese.json, british.json and general.json - trap 7 on all three.

FORTUNE FRIED CHICKEN - THIRD at the 2026 Championships, sister brand to Gunpowder, and ALREADY RECORDED IN thai.json. It may legitimately sit in both corpora; its thai.json count must never be printed here.

GOOD FRIEND CHICKEN - already in chinese.json, and named by five sources here. Two spellings in play: 'Good Friend' (Standard, Infatuation) and 'Good Friend Chicken' (Time Out, Eater, SquareMeal). Alias before recording or it splits into two weakly-supported venues.

'CHICKEN SHOP' THE BRAND VERSUS 'chicken shop' THE CATEGORY. Soho House's Chicken Shop is named by SquareMeal and ranked 11th by The London Economic. It is a ROTISSERIE, so it probably fails the fried test - and separately, once norm() strips to [a-z0-9] it will collide with the category word used throughout the guide. Two different problems on one name.

'FAVOURITE' VERSUS 'FAVORITE CHICKEN & RIBS'. The London Economic ranks 'Favourite' fifth; chickenbible spells it the American way twice. The British chain is Favourite. Alias it, and treat the US spelling as a farm tell rather than a variant.

CHEEMC IS TIME OUT'S NUMBER ONE and it is already in korean.json under two names ('CheeMC' from DesignMyNight, 'CheeMc Soho' and 'CheeMc' from LondonBest). Alias all three. Trap 7: its Korean count must not appear here. See theOverlapFinding for the migrate-or-leave decision.

WINGSTOP, POPEYES, SLIM CHICKENS, THUNDERBIRD, ABSURD BIRD - multi-branch chains, several American. chains.json handling. Absurd Bird was ranked ninth by The London Economic in 2023 and its current London presence needs checking before it is printed.

WING FEST'S WINNERS NEED ADDRESSES BEFORE THEY NEED CITATIONS. Peck Peck, Ginger Wings, Mexican Seoul, Greidy's Wings & Strips, Mollis, Bare Bones, Djangos Smokehouse, Hot Chick, KYR Kitchen, Jus' Winging It, Kell's Kitchen. Establish which have a permanent London site; a pop-up that traded at one festival is not a place to send a reader.
CHICK KING versus CHICK-KING (Ideal Magazine hyphenates it) - alias. And Rooster's Hut appears only in Eater (2022) and Secret London (2023), both stale; confirm it is still trading before it counts.
